strings.d1.s0.name: Petronas Twin Towers Skybridge
strings.d1.s0.tips: Skybridge on the 41st floor plus the 86th-floor observation deck (~98 MYR). Tickets sell out online days ahead, so book the first morning slot.
strings.d1.s1.name: KLCC Park
strings.d1.s1.tips: Park and fountain at the foot of the towers; the best spot for photos of them.
strings.d1.s2.name: Nasi Lemak Wanjo Kampung Baru
strings.d1.s2.tips: A nasi lemak classic in Kampung Baru, with sambal and chicken, within walking distance of KLCC.
strings.d1.s3.name: Kampung Baru
strings.d1.s3.tips: A Malay village in the middle of the skyscrapers, with wooden houses and street stalls.
strings.d1.s4.name: KL Tower Sky Deck
strings.d1.s4.tips: Menara KL's glass box and sunset views; the best place to see the Petronas Towers from across the city.
strings.d1.b0.name: Suria KLCC Signatures Food Court
strings.d1.b0.tips: Mall food court; try the laksa and satay.
strings.d1.b1.name: Aquaria KLCC
strings.d1.b1.tips: Aquarium beneath the convention centre; a good rainy-day option.
strings.d2.s0.name: Batu Caves
strings.d2.s0.tips: 30 minutes by KTM train. 272 colourful steps, a giant Murugan statue, and monkeys to watch out for. Cool and quiet in the morning.
strings.d2.s1.name: Petaling Street
strings.d2.s1.tips: Chinatown market with fake designer bags and street food; haggle.
strings.d2.s2.name: Hong Kee Claypot Chicken Rice
strings.d2.s2.tips: Charcoal-cooked claypot rice on Petaling Street; expect a queue at lunch.
strings.d2.s3.name: Sri Mahamariamman Temple
strings.d2.s3.tips: KL's oldest Hindu temple, with a colourful gopuram.
strings.d2.s4.name: Central Market Kuala Lumpur
strings.d2.s4.tips: Art deco market selling batik and handicrafts, and air-conditioned.
strings.d2.b0.name: Kim Lian Kee Hokkien Mee
strings.d2.b0.tips: Hokkien mee since 1927, on Petaling Street.
strings.d2.b1.name: Guan Di Temple
strings.d3.s0.name: Merdeka Square
strings.d3.s0.tips: Independence square and the Sultan Abdul Samad Building; lovely in morning light.
strings.d3.s1.name: Masjid Jamek
strings.d3.s1.tips: Moorish-style mosque where two rivers meet; admire it from outside during non-visiting hours.
strings.d3.s2.name: River of Life Walk
strings.d3.s2.tips: Restored riverside walkway along the Klang, with blue-lit fountains.
strings.d3.s3.name: Islamic Arts Museum Malaysia
strings.d3.s3.tips: Asia's best Islamic art museum: air-conditioned, with domes and calligraphy.
strings.d3.s4.name: Jalan Alor
strings.d3.s4.tips: Bukit Bintang's street food strip: grilled seafood, satay and char kway teow. It comes alive in the evening.
strings.d3.b0.name: Pavilion KL Food Court
strings.d3.b0.tips: Food court in the Bukit Bintang mall; good in the rain.
strings.d3.b1.name: Perdana Botanical Garden
strings.d3.b1.tips: The city's botanical park, with an orchid garden; an alternative to the museum.
strings.d4.s0.name: Brickfields Little India
strings.d4.s0.tips: Colourful Indian neighbourhood with temples and flower garlands.
strings.d4.s1.name: Thean Hou Temple
strings.d4.s1.tips: Six-tier Chinese temple on a hilltop, with red lanterns and city views.
strings.d4.s2.name: Vishal Food & Catering Brickfields
strings.d4.s2.tips: South Indian food served on a banana leaf; eat with your hands.
strings.d4.s3.name: Bangsar Village
strings.d4.s3.tips: Stylish neighbourhood with cafés and boutiques.
strings.d4.s4.name: Bangsar Devi's Corner
strings.d4.s4.tips: Roti canai and teh tarik at a 24-hour mamak.
strings.d4.b0.name: Thean Hou Vegetarian Canteen
strings.d4.b1.name: National Museum of Malaysia
strings.d4.b1.tips: National museum on Malaysian history; good in the rain.
strings.d5.s0.name: Dutch Square Melaka
strings.d5.s0.tips: 2 hours by bus from KL (~15 MYR). Red Stadthuys and Christ Church, UNESCO-listed.
strings.d5.s1.name: A Famosa
strings.d5.s1.tips: The gate of the Portuguese fort and St. Paul's Hill, with views over the Strait of Malacca.
strings.d5.s2.name: Jonker Street
strings.d5.s2.tips: Peranakan antique shops and cafés; night market at weekends.
strings.d5.s3.name: Hoe Kee Chicken Rice Ball
strings.d5.s3.tips: Melaka's signature chicken rice, with rice shaped into balls; the queue moves fast.
strings.d5.s4.name: Baba & Nyonya Heritage Museum
strings.d5.s4.tips: Peranakan mansion, visited on a guided tour.
strings.d5.b0.name: Nancy's Kitchen Melaka
strings.d5.b0.tips: Nyonya cuisine; try the ayam pongteh.
strings.d5.b1.name: Melaka River Cruise
strings.d5.b1.tips: River boat ride; an alternative to the museum.
strings.d6.s0.name: Genting Skyway
strings.d6.s0.tips: From Awana, one of the world's longest cable cars climbs to 1,800 m. Enjoy the cool mountain air and a stop at Chin Swee Temple.
strings.d6.s1.name: Genting SkyAvenue Food Court
strings.d6.s1.tips: Food court in the mall on the mountain.
strings.d6.s2.name: Chin Swee Caves Temple
strings.d6.s2.tips: Taoist temple on a cliff, at the cable car's mid-station.
strings.d6.s3.name: Skytropolis Genting
strings.d6.s3.tips: Indoor theme park, unaffected by rain.
strings.d6.b0.name: Kuala Selangor Seafood Restaurant
strings.d6.b1.name: Sekinchan Rice Fields
strings.d6.b1.tips: Rice fields near Kuala Selangor; best in harvest season.
strings.d7.s0.name: Masjid Negara
strings.d7.s0.tips: National mosque with a blue star-shaped dome; robes are lent to visitors during visiting hours.
strings.d7.s1.name: Kuala Lumpur Railway Station
strings.d7.s1.tips: Historic Moorish-style station; good for photos.
strings.d7.s2.name: Restoran Yut Kee
strings.d7.s2.tips: Hainan coffee and roti babi since 1928; a fitting farewell lunch.
strings.d7.s3.name: KL Sentral
strings.d7.s3.tips: KLIA Ekspres takes 28 minutes; time to say goodbye.
strings.d7.b0.name: Restoran Nasi Kandar Pelita
strings.d7.b1.name: KL Bird Park
strings.d7.b1.tips: The world's largest free-flight walk-in aviary; an alternative to the mosque.
strings.note0: Use a Touch 'n Go card for the LRT and MRT; Grab taxis are cheap (5-15 MYR within the city). The KLIA Ekspres takes 28 minutes and costs 55 MYR.
strings.note1: Summer (June-September) is relatively dry, but expect 33°C and humidity. Afternoon downpours are common, so sightsee in the morning.
strings.note2: Malaysian food blends three cultures: nasi lemak (Malay), char kway teow (Chinese) and roti canai (Indian). Mamak restaurants are open 24 hours.
strings.note3: Shoulders and knees must be covered in mosques and Hindu temples. At Batu Caves, monkeys snatch bags.
strings.note4: Petronas Skybridge tickets sell out days ahead; KL Tower is an alternative with better views.
strings.note5: Alcohol is expensive because of tax. Tipping is not expected, and a 10% service charge is added.
strings.transit.name: Touch 'n Go Card
strings.transit.why_chosen: Works on the LRT, MRT, monorail and buses; the KLIA Ekspres is separate
